en: I wonder when I'll finally be able\nto return to Earth.
To tell you the truth, I have\nchildren I left behind on Earth.
Oh, ah, no, I didn't actually give\nbirth to them! I'm still single!!
Actually, I volunteer to look\nafter children living in a facility\non Earth.
I just can't stop worrying about\nthem...
I want to see them all... I\nwonder how they're doing right\nnow...
Until I boarded this ship, I had\nonly ever been to my home\nplanet and Earth.
That's why, in a way, I'm\nactually quite enjoying this\njourney.
Was that a bit insensitive? I'm\nsorry.
But... I have a feeling that\nyou're enjoying this journey\ntoo, Eve.
Why do you think that?
You look like you have a lot on\nyour mind, though.
It's because she's in love with\nme.
I have no proof... but my\nintuition is usually spot on.
Well, she is a Girl, so she must\nhave plenty of worries.

Even I have things like wanting
to lose the fat in my chubby
cheeks... or doing something
about my thighs...

But whenever I tell a man
these things, they say things
like, "A little extra weight looks
good on you!"
Even though you don't actually\nmean it!! Captain, you idiot!!!
I-Is that so...? Ahahaha,\nhahahahaha...
Sometimes, being kind means\nknowing when not to bring\nthings up.
If you'll pardon my intrusion...
Didn't your stomach growl\nduring the battle?
You see, I actually love\ncooking!
So, I can't help but worry about\nwhether the people around me\nare hungry or not.

See, food made in an
automatic cooker is delicious,
but it lacks character, doesn't
it?
After a battle, when you're all\nsweaty, something a little salty\njust tastes better.
Making those kinds of\nadjustments is hard for a\nmachine, right?
If there's anything you want to\neat, just let me know. I'll show\nyou what I can do!
I wonder how the children are\ndoing...
Sorry, I spaced out for a\nmoment. I just can't stop\nthinking about Earth.
You know, like I told you\nbefore, about that orphanage\nfor war orphans on Earth.
The children at that facility are\naround ten years old now,
and since I had already lost my\nparents by that age...
I think I understand the\nloneliness they must feel...
But, hey! Look at me, I grew up\nperfectly healthy!
I know the children will be just\nfine, too.
It's just... I just want to see\nthem... that's all...
You've been through a lot.
I'm sure those children want to\nsee you, too.
You're their mother, Miki.
Oh, it wasn't really that much\nof a struggle.

On our planet, there were
many children without parents,
and many parents who lost
their children...

But still, I can't help but
imagine what they would say if
their mother were here right
now.
Thank you for your concern.
...Please, don't say things like\nthat!
Ah, it's making me feel so\nhomesick!!
I want to see those kids right\nthis second!!
Let's go home quickly! To\nEarth! Hurry!!
Ugh, do I really look that\nmeddlesome?
My former traveling\ncompanions used to say that\nto me all the time...
I don't need a womanizer\nwho's a handful like a\n40-year-old child!
I mentioned before that I lost\nmy parents when I was young,\nright?
Ah, please don't look so\ngloomy.
I wasn't a pitiful child at all.

Around the same time my
parents passed away, my
childhood friend's mother
passed away too.

My childhood friend was a
Boy... well, even though I call
him a child, he's actually older
than me.
...We grew up together like real\nsiblings.

Well, for me... becoming siblings
wasn't exactly a good thing; it
was more complicated than
that...
Anyway, enough about that!!
He always used to praise me,\nsaying my cooking was even\nbetter than his mother's...
She was actually such an\namazing cook.
She used to create a place\nwhere I belonged. She truly\nwas my second family.
That's why I know.
That the bond between parent\nand child can be about so\nmuch more than just blood.
Fighting helps clear my head a\nlittle! It's like... a way to vent\nstress!

Lately, I've been thinking about
the children at the Earth
facilities and my parents, who
passed away when I was
young.
And it just leaves me feeling...\nunsettled.

Like I'm on the verge of
remembering something, but I
can't. Like a sneeze that won't
come out. That's the feeling.
It's as if I've forgotten\nsomething incredibly important\nabout my mother...

Memories from when you're a
small child are so hazy; even
when you try to recall them,
it's like grasping at clouds...
Do you ever feel that way,\nCaptain?
I know that feeling all too well.
Don't dwell on the past.
When I was young, I was\nfamous as a child prodigy...
You really were!
In my case, I usually relieve my\naccumulated stress through\ncooking.
But lately, I've been thinking\ncombat is pretty great too! So,\nplease let me go wild!
Is that so? Maybe I should do\nthe same.
But once I start worrying about\nsomething, I can't stop!
Was that the case!!
I know a woman who is just like\nthat.
But, she's... a bit eccentric.
Her taste in clothes... and her\ntaste in romance...
Could it be, Captain, that you\nare also...
N-no way, that can't be true!\nAhahaha, ahahahahaha...
Eh? There was a suspicious\nperson rampaging in the\nkitchen last night!?
U-um, well... I don't think it's\npossible for anyone to break in\nfrom the outside.
Could it be that AI-kun ran out\nof machine oil and was looking\nfor cooking oil in the kitchen?
Oh, so that was a report from\nAI-kun... In that case, um...
Ugh, I'm sorry. I'm the culprit...

Last night, I couldn't sleep
because I was lost in thought
about my mother again, and I
couldn't remember...

I thought moving my body
would tire me out so I could
sleep, so I ended up kneading
pie dough night after night.
I'm sorry for causing such a\ncommotion...

I mean, well... kneading pie
dough just to get some
exercise is a bit strange, I
guess...
But for some reason, in that\nmoment, I just thought, "This is\nit!"
Since it's a dish I never\nnormally make,
I honestly made it with the\nmindset of, "I might as well just\nfail!"...
Would you like to come try\nsome later? ...I can't guarantee\nhow it tastes, though...
I'd love to come try it!
I'm not very good with pie.
His last words were that he\ncouldn't stand pie.
I have plenty of it, so please,\nhave a serving!
Men who can eat a lot are\nquite cool, after all!
...Maybe I should prepare a few\nother things too.
There are quite a few people\nwho don't like foods with a\nmushy texture.
Well then, maybe next time I'll\ntry making something that\ngoes down smoothly?
Pudding or jelly might be good.
What kind of last words are\nthose!?
Fine then. I'm sure you wouldn't\nwant to eat food made in a\nfrantic rush every single night.
I'll eat it all by myself. There\nare 16 plates, but I'm not\ngiving any to you, Captain!
Please listen! Captain!
Ever since then, I've become\nobsessed with making pies.\nAnd listen to this!
It's Eve! The one and only Eve\nis helping me!
Surprising, right!? And she's\nactually quite a natural at it,\ntoo.
It really made me realize that\nEve is, after all, just a girl!

I'm thinking that next time,
while we make pies together, I
might try to get her to tell me
some love stories.
Even if you're curious, I won't\ntell you! It's a maiden's secret.
While I was making pies with\nEve... I felt like something like\nthis had happened before.
That I had been baking pies\nwith someone...
And that's when it all came\nback to me!

I loved the pies my mother
used to make, and we used to
bake them together all the
time.
I probably didn't help out that\nmuch, but...
My mother would always praise\nme...
That's why I loved her pies\neven more...
The reason I avoided baking\nthem, and the reason I didn't\nwant to eat them...
Was because I didn't want\nanything other than my\nmother's pies.
In the process, I ended up\nforgetting so many things...
I'm glad I remembered.
From now on, I'm going to bake\npies like crazy!

I hate to toot my own horn, but
they're actually quite delicious.
Please, have some with me
next time.
One batch of the Soeversta\nfamily's special pies is ready to\ngo!!
Eat them while they're still hot!

I'm glad you like it! My heart
was racing because I was so
worried you might say it tastes
bad.
There's plenty more, so please,\nkeep eating.
There's one more thing I\nremembered about my mother.
She used to say it all the time.

If your stomach is full, that
alone is enough to make you
happy.	machine
